campo-conquest.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 169 (transcribed from the page image)
campo-conquest.quote: Le 2e, destiné à faire la conquête des Calabres, se composait de 12,632 hommes de toutes armes avec 12 bouches à feu, dont 6 de montagne, et fut mis sous les ordres du général Reynier.
campo-conquest.english_rendering: The second corps was assigned the conquest of Calabria. The accompanying strength is contextual and is not adopted as an opening count.

campo-attack-order.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 173 (transcribed from the page image)
campo-attack-order.quote: Conformément à ce qui fut arrêté dans un conseil présidé par Joseph, et où assista Massena, on convint que Reynier attaquerait le corps de gauche pendant que Duhesme aborderait celui de droite.
campo-attack-order.english_rendering: A council chaired by Joseph with Masséna present agreed that Reynier would attack the left corps while Duhesme engaged the right.

campo-attack-result.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 175
campo-attack-result.quote: Les redoutes sont bientôt abordées; leurs défenseurs, voyant les Français couronner les hauteurs que le général Damas avait jugées d'un accès presque inaccessible, répondent par quelques coups de canon mal dirigés aux premières décharges de mousqueterie, abandonnent les redoutes et s'enfuient sur la première ligne.
campo-attack-result.english_rendering: The redoubts were attacked and their defenders abandoned them for the first line, in Koch's account.

campo-later-pursuit.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 176 (transcribed from the page image)
campo-later-pursuit.quote: Reynier, ne voulant pas laisser au général Damas le temps de s'établir dans les gorges qui auraient pu favoriser la jonction des débris de son corps avec celui de droite encore intact, se porta de Morano le 10 au matin sur Castro Villari,
campo-later-pursuit.english_rendering: Reynier moved on the following morning to prevent a possible junction. This is a later aim, not proof of the objective before the Campo Tenese action.

campo-delay-plan.locator: Memoirs of the Comte Roger de Damas (1913), p. 393 (transcribed from the page image)
campo-delay-plan.quote: Here I intended to place my recruits, supposing the enemy were successful in all the first encounters and it should become necessary to hold this position for a day or two, while the two wings were effecting a junction on the banks of the Coscile or the Crati.
campo-delay-plan.english_rendering: Damas intended to hold this position for a day or two, if earlier encounters failed, while the wings joined on the Coscile or Crati.

campo-junction-plan.locator: Memoirs of the Comte Roger de Damas (1913), p. 395 (transcribed from the page image)
campo-junction-plan.quote: It became necessary for my right wing to retire without delay; and the position of Campo Tenese, which I had fortified and furnished with artillery, I determined to use in the way I have already described, to check the enemy with my left and effect a junction of the two wings.
campo-junction-plan.english_rendering: Damas says he decided to use Campo Tenese to check the enemy with his left and join the two wings.

campo-retreat.locator: Memoirs of the Comte Roger de Damas (1787-1806); printed p. 396
campo-retreat.quote: I gave the order to retire, and tried to effect a methodical retreat, but the fog was so thick that I could not see nor control the movement of the troops. A portion of them lost their way in the mist, and several battalions fell into the enemy's hands. I returned, with those that had been able to carry out my orders, to the appointed position on the banks of the Crati.¹³
campo-retreat.english_rendering: Damas reports ordering retirement, losing control of parts of it and returning with some troops to the appointed Crati position.

campo-partial-junction.locator: Damas (1913), p. 396; full OCR selection, checked against the pinned p. 396 image
campo-partial-junction.quote: The general, indeed, joined me with some of his troops, but was in so great a hurry to be safe that he had broken down the bridge between himself and his advanced guard, sending a message to the officer-in-command to cross the river by a bridge much lower down.
campo-partial-junction.english_rendering: Damas reports that the general joined him with some troops, but had broken the bridge between those troops and the advanced guard.
campo-partial-junction.note: This paragraph is omitted from the old figure transcription; the existing full OCR selection is cited unchanged and the existing page image was inspected.

campo-unjoined-guard.locator: Damas (1913), p. 396; full OCR selection, checked against the pinned p. 396 image
campo-unjoined-guard.quote: So much time was lost in reaching the other that the commanding-officer thought it was too late to make any attempt at joining the army-corps, though there was nothing whatever to give rise to this opinion. He therefore retreated, by the road that skirts the Ionian Sea, to Catrone;
campo-unjoined-guard.english_rendering: The advanced-guard commander judged joining too late and withdrew toward Catrone, in Damas's account. The author's criticism is retained as his opinion.
campo-unjoined-guard.note: The OCR hyphenation is preserved. No all-wing force total or effective command mapping is inferred.

campo-afterward-judgment.locator: Memoirs of the Comte Roger de Damas (1913), p. 397 (transcribed from the page image)
campo-afterward-judgment.quote: Not that there was now any hope of holding the Calabrian Provinces for long; but the ground might have been disputed inch by inch. This was the only possible object of the campaign, since the population refused to make any resistance.
campo-afterward-judgment.english_rendering: Damas comments after the reverse that the ground might have been disputed inch by inch and calls that the only possible campaign object. This is retrospective/counterfactual commentary.

calabria-exceptions.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 177 (OCR page boundaries; not checked against print)
calabria-exceptions.quote: Nous étions alors maîtres de tout le pays , à l'exception d' Amantea et de Maratea, dont les gamiscms ne succombèrent que quelques mois plus tard.
calabria-exceptions.english_rendering: Koch reports control of the country at that stage except Amantea and Maratea. This describes a later campaign state, not the Campo Tenese battlefield alone.

maida-french-intent.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 189 (transcribed from the page image)
maida-french-intent.quote: Soit que Reynier, qui n'avait pas été heureux en Egypte dans une rencontre avec Stewart, crût, dit-on, avoir trouvé l'occasion de prendre sa revanche, soit que les bandes qui l'avaient harcelé pendant sa marche lui fissent craindre de voir sa communication avec ses magasins coupée, il résolut d'attaquer, malgré l'infériorité de ses forces, ne doutant pas qu'après avoir forcé le général anglais à se rembarquer, il n'eût bon marché des
maida-french-intent.english_rendering: Koch reports a decision to attack and the expectation of forcing the English general to re-embark. His alternative revenge/communications explanations are speculative; neither is adopted as an established motive.

maida-french-retreat.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 190
maida-french-retreat.quote: Vainement Reynier fait exécuter plusieurs charges de cavalerie contre les batteries anglaises, la bataille est perdue sans retour. Il ordonna alors la retraite, et elle s'effectua en ordre par les hauteurs de Tiriolo sur Catanzaro, couverte par le général Franceschi avec le 20e et les chasseurs du 9e.
maida-french-retreat.english_rendering: Koch reports failed attacks and a French retreat through the Tiriolo heights toward Catanzaro. His date of the action on p. 189 differs from the frozen entry/Bunbury; no date is silently corrected.

maida-expected-chain.locator: Bunbury (1854), p. 235 (transcribed from the page image)
maida-expected-chain.quote: But weighing the question on both sides, we came to believe that if we could make good our landing with 5000 men in the Gulf of St. Eufemia, Reynier would find it necessary to retreat to Catanzaro; that the insurrection of both the provinces would then become general, and that Massena would be obliged to abandon the siege of Gaeta.
maida-expected-chain.english_rendering: Bunbury recalls a conditional belief: a landing would force Reynier toward Catanzaro, generalize the insurrection in both provinces and oblige Masséna to abandon the siege of Gaëta. These are separate expected consequences.

maida-camp-order.locator: Bunbury (1854), p. 240 (transcribed from the page image)
maida-camp-order.quote: In consequence of the observations made this evening, an order was issued for the march of the troops at daylight on the morning of the 4th, with the declared purpose of attacking the enemy's camp.
maida-camp-order.english_rendering: Bunbury says an order was issued that evening to march at daylight on the fourth with the declared purpose of attacking the enemy camp. This is a later narrative of an order, not the surviving dated order itself.

maida-left-plan.locator: Bunbury (1854), p. 241 (transcribed from the page image)
maida-left-plan.quote: The object of our advance was to gain the left of the French position which was clearly their weak point; for to say the truth we gave little heed to the reports which stated the enemy to be stronger in numbers than ourselves.
maida-left-plan.english_rendering: Bunbury describes the object of the advance as gaining the left of the French position.

maida-position-moved.locator: Narratives of some passages in the great war with France, from 1799 to 1810; printed p. 241
maida-position-moved.quote: A detachment of the enemy's light cavalry retired as we drew near; and just as our two columns opened into the lower part of the plain of Maida, we descried the French army filing by its right from the position in which it had bivouacked on the high ground and descending into the upper portion of the same plain.
maida-position-moved.english_rendering: Bunbury reports the British advancing and seeing the French leave their bivouac position for the plain; literal attainment of the originally intended camp/flank geometry is not established by victory.

maida-catanzaro-result.locator: Narratives of some passages in the great war with France, from 1799 to 1810; printed p. 254
maida-catanzaro-result.quote: This prospect again was frustrated by the happy accident of the landing of our 20th Regiment, and their rapid and unexpected attack on the right of the French line. Reynier then, beaten back in the direction which his left wing had taken in its flight, made his retreat at once by the road towards Catanzaro.
maida-catanzaro-result.english_rendering: Bunbury reports Reynier retreating toward Catanzaro after the defeat. This supports the direction of retreat; arrival time and causal attribution to the landing alone remain unestablished.

maida-left-result.locator: Bunbury (1854), p. 254 (transcribed from the page image)
maida-left-result.quote: This early overthrow of Reynier's left wing put an end to his hope of destroying us, but still left him a fair chance of making it a drawn battle on his right, and of maintaining a hold on the country.
maida-left-result.english_rendering: Bunbury says the early overthrow of Reynier's left ended his hope of destroying the British. The passage does not prove the planned geographical envelopment occurred.

maida-limited-insurrection.locator: Koch, t. V (1850), OCR p. 246, gaeta-capitulation
maida-limited-insurrection.quote: Le comn^miant Hotz, qui connaissait les résultats du débarquement de Santa Bufemia, et qui savait que Tinsurrection des CSalabres se bornait à fat Basilicate, fut ébranlé par cette proposition, mais ae Taccqrta pas.
maida-limited-insurrection.english_rendering: Koch later describes the insurrection as limited to Basilicata while reporting Hotz's response to an evacuation offer. The OCR and geographical/scope wording remain qualified; this does not establish the extent of both provinces independently.
maida-limited-insurrection.note: OCR-only: no pinned page 246 image exists in the allowed source set. No corrected quotation or normalized geographical coverage is supplied.

gaeta-capture-intent.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 211 (transcribed from the page image)
gaeta-capture-intent.quote: Les Anglais pouvant arriver subitement sur les côtes, Joseph, devenu roi, sentit plus que jamais la nécessité de se rendre maître de Gaëte.
gaeta-capture-intent.english_rendering: Koch attributes to Joseph an increased need to master Gaëta because the British could arrive suddenly on the coast.

gaeta-accelerate-and-release.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), p. 28 (transcribed from the page image)
gaeta-accelerate-and-release.quote: Il re piegando al più debole partito, Saliceti al più forte, fu deciso che, doppiando mezzi e fatiche di guerra, si accelerasse la resa di Gaeta, onde valersi nelle ribellate province di quattordicimila soldati, oppugnatori di quella fortezza, e che subito vi fusse spedito il Maresciallo Massena, del quale la fama e l'ingegno apportassero aiuto ed animo a'suoi, danno e sgomento al nemico.
gaeta-accelerate-and-release.english_rendering: Colletta reports a council decision to hasten Gaëta's surrender so that the besieging troops could be used in the rebellious provinces. The stated number is not a verified redeployment count.

gaeta-surrender.locator: Storia del Reame di Napoli dal 1734 sino al 1825, di Pietro Colletta; con una notizia intorno alla vita dell'autore scritta da Gino Capponi, volume secondo; printed p. 28
gaeta-surrender.quote: Gaeta si arrese a'18 dello stesso luglio.
gaeta-surrender.english_rendering: Colletta reports Gaëta surrendering on the eighteenth of that July.

gaeta-entry.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 248
gaeta-entry.quote: Les Français entrèrent dans Gaëte le 19, à 4 heures du matin; les colonnes des généraux Donzelot et Valentin y pénétrèrent par les brèches.
gaeta-entry.english_rendering: Koch reports French entry on the nineteenth at four in the morning. Agreement and physical entry are separate events; the clock is source-qualified.

gaeta-terms.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 420
gaeta-terms.quote: En considération de la valeureuse défense de la garnison de Gaëte, il lui est permis de s'embarquer avec armes et bagages sous condition expresse que les corps qui la composent ne pourront servir contre la France ou ses alliés, ni contre Sa Majesté le roi Joseph Napoléon, avant un an et un jour, soit sur le continent, soit dans les îles.
gaeta-terms.english_rendering: The printed translated capitulation permits embarkation with arms and baggage subject to one year and one day of non-service. Legal terms do not establish later compliance or permanent force destruction.

gaeta-instrument-date.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 422
gaeta-instrument-date.quote: Ce 18 juillet 1806 à 11 heures du soir.
gaeta-instrument-date.english_rendering: The printed capitulation is dated eighteenth July 1806 at eleven at night. This dates the outcome instrument, not a prior objective or appointment.

gaeta-translation-note.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 422
gaeta-translation-note.english_rendering: The printed instrument is described as translated from the Italian original. The original manuscript was not inspected; this is not another independent source family.

gaeta-evacuation-report.locator: Storia del Reame di Napoli dal 1734 sino al 1825, di Pietro Colletta; con una notizia intorno alla vita dell'autore scritta da Gino Capponi, volume secondo; printed p. 30
gaeta-evacuation-report.quote: Fu concordato in quel giorno istesso rendere Gaeta a'Francesi ed imbarcare la guernigione per Sicilia, prima giurando di non combattere contro la Francia ed i suoi confederati per un anno ed un giorno.
gaeta-evacuation-report.english_rendering: Colletta reports agreement that day to surrender Gaëta and embark the garrison for Sicily under a non-service oath. This is not a pre-action garrison objective.

gaeta-council-hold.locator: Koch, t. V (1850), OCR pp. 242–243, gaeta-governor; continuation of the sentence about the acting commander
gaeta-council-hold.quote: oîqner la lettre du œarédial la soumet à un conseil de guerre, dont la migcsité est d'avis de tenir encore dix4iait jours*
gaeta-council-hold.english_rendering: Koch reports the letter being put to a war council whose majority favors holding longer. The following duration is garbled in this OCR; no normalized number of days is adopted.
gaeta-council-hold.note: OCR-only; pinned pp. 242–243 images are absent. Literal duration dix4iait jours* is retained, with numeric duration null. The prior dossier quotation stopped before that duration.

gaeta-early-refusal.locator: Colletta, vol. II (1856), OCR p. 12, fortresses-1806
gaeta-early-refusal.quote: Gaeta si apprestò alle difese perciocché il principe di Philipstadt, che ne teneva il gover- no , rispose alla reggenza che egli disobbediva al comando di lei, per comandi maggiori e onor di guerra.
gaeta-early-refusal.english_rendering: Colletta reports the governor refusing the regency's surrender direction under higher commands and honor. The actual prior order, timing and a common success horizon are not supplied.
gaeta-early-refusal.note: OCR-only; no pinned p. 12 image. Do not reconcile Philipstadt/Hotz/Storz identities or infer an exclusive whole-siege appointment.

gaeta-reflective-motive.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 249 (transcribed from the page image)
gaeta-reflective-motive.quote: Ils débutèrent par une maladresse : la roideur des procédés du général Lacour, dans son entrevue avec les fondés de pouvoir du prince de Hesse, détermina ce dernier à défendre la place, ce qu'il n'avait peut-être pas l'intention de faire d'abord.
gaeta-reflective-motive.english_rendering: Koch later speculates that Lacour's manner determined the prince to defend, which he perhaps had not initially intended. This alternative to Colletta's higher-command explanation is retained, not reconciled.

amantea-renewed-attack.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 281 (transcribed from the page image)
amantea-renewed-attack.quote: Cependant il fallait en finir : le maréchal se rendit le 15 décembre à Cosenza, où il arrêta les dernières dispositions concernant l'attaque d'Amantea.
amantea-renewed-attack.english_rendering: Koch says that on fifteenth December the marshal settled the final dispositions for the attack on Amantea, after earlier failures. The marshal's role is not converted into sole siege credit.

amantea-earlier-order.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 280
amantea-earlier-order.quote: Tranquille sur ce point, Verdier, conformément aux ordres du maréchal, partit de Cosenza le 3 décembre pour réduire Amantea, à la tête de 1,300 hommes, 2 obusiers et 2 pièces de montagne.
amantea-earlier-order.english_rendering: Koch reports an earlier order to reduce Amantea and a departure on third December. It belongs to an earlier attempt, not the frozen eighteenth-December investment by assumption.

amantea-capitulation.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, rédigés d'après les documents qu'il a laissés et sur ceux du dépôt de la guerre et du dépôt des fortifications, tome V (campaigns of 1805 in Italy, 1806 in Naples and 1807); printed p. 282
amantea-capitulation.quote: Plusieurs assauts ayant été repoussés, il fallut entrer en galerie, et ce ne fut que le 6 février, après 33 jours de siége, que la place capitula. Reynier accorda à la garnison la faculté de passer en Sicile, à condition de ne pas servir contre nous pendant un an et un jour.
amantea-capitulation.english_rendering: Koch reports capitulation on sixth February after a source-stated thirty-three siege days, with conditional passage to Sicily. The source's siege duration is not automatically measured from the frozen entry start.

amantea-peace-condition.locator: Koch, Mémoires de Masséna, t. V, p. 278 (OCR page boundaries; not checked against print)
amantea-peace-condition.quote: Mais aax eavf- rons de La^negro, de CSosenza et sur la <AtQ da ^olfe de Policastro ^ il n'y avait pas d'espoir de ramener k paix tant que Maratea et Amaatea seraient entre les mains des Anglo-Siciliens.
amantea-peace-condition.english_rendering: The OCR attributes a necessary condition for restoring peace to reducing the towns in Anglo-Sicilian hands. It does not establish that capturing one town would be sufficient for pacification.

amantea-resistance.locator: Storia del Reame di Napoli dal 1734 sino al 1825, di Pietro Colletta; con una notizia intorno alla vita dell'autore scritta da Gino Capponi, volume secondo; printed p. 32
amantea-resistance.quote: Il generale, poi che vidde non bastare le sorprese, non gl'inganni, non le forze, levato l'assedio, ritornò doglioso ed assetato di vendetta in Cosenza.
amantea-resistance.english_rendering: Colletta reports the earlier siege being lifted after unsuccessful attempts. His judgments are authorial; the first attempt is not assigned to an invented common clock.

amantea-fidelity.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), p. 33 (transcribed from the page image)
amantea-fidelity.quote: al quale giungendo al campo amorevolmente scrisse, e questi amorevolmente rispose, l'un l'altro tentandosi, l'Amato con esaltare l'amor di patria, il Mirabelli la virtù della fede, ed in entrambi prevalendo l'onore, durarono nemici no, ma contrarii.
amantea-fidelity.english_rendering: Colletta describes an exchange between Amato and Mirabelli, the latter appealing to fidelity, and their remaining opposed. This is evidence of a disposition, not a specified operational mandate or deadline.

amantea-hunger-surrender.locator: Colletta, Storia del Reame di Napoli, vol. II (1856), p. 33 (transcribed from the page image)
amantea-hunger-surrender.quote: Ma soprastava la fame a'Calabresi, e sol per essa il piccolo castello di Amantea, munito di tre rosi cannoni, difeso da inesperti partigiani, assalito da fortissime schiere con le migliori arti di guerra, dopo quaranta giorni di assedio (senza tener conto del primo assalto) a patti onorevoli si arrese.
amantea-hunger-surrender.english_rendering: Colletta attributes surrender on honorable terms after forty siege days, excluding the first assault, to hunger. This is his causal account, not an estimated effect or an interchangeable duration with Koch's thirty-three.

gaeta-royal-injunction.locator: Colletta, vol. II (1856), OCR p. 12, fortresses-1806; paragraph preceding Gaeta's refusal
gaeta-royal-injunction.quote: Perciò la paurosa reggenza concordò per ambasciatori , come ho narrato nel precedente libro, rimettere al nemico le fortezze, i castelh, i luoghi for- tificati, trasgredendo il comando lasciatole dal re Ferdinando di non mai cedere (qualunque fosse la estremità dei casi) le fortezze del Regno.
gaeta-royal-injunction.english_rendering: Colletta says the regency's surrender of fortresses contravened Ferdinand's instruction never to cede royal fortresses, whatever the extremity. This is a general instruction to the regency, not automatically a settled Gaeta commander-specific mission.
gaeta-royal-injunction.note: OCR-only; no allowed pinned p. 12 image. Distinguish the royal/regency instruction, Gaeta's refusal and the later local council. No command-identity or effective-tenure decision is made.

components.objective: Attack the opposing left corps as agreed by the council.
components.precedence_note: Koch places the council agreement before the advance and action; the original dated order is not supplied.
components.observed_result: Koch reports the attack on the redoubts and the defenders abandoning them.
components.result_window: Campo Tenese action in Koch's narrative.
limits: Execution of an ordered attack is not a measure of its strategic value.
The dossier's phrase destroying the corps is stronger than this quoted attack directive.
components.criterion_note: An attack on that corps is reported.

components.precedence_note: Koch places the assignment in the organization preceding the march.
components.observed_result: Koch later reports control except Amantea and Maratea; this is a qualified wider state.
components.result_window: The later stage of the March advance described in the source.
limits: The exception towns and later state cannot be credited solely to Campo Tenese.
No operational appointment, persistent army or full campaign endpoint is selected.
components.criterion_note: No extent, permanence or campaign endpoint is specified.

components.objective: Hold Campo Tenese for a day or two if needed to cover the wings' junction.
components.precedence_note: Damas recounts his plan before describing the ninth-March attack.
components.observed_result: Damas reports withdrawing to the Crati with some troops; the passages do not measure the delay actually obtained.
components.result_window: Campo Tenese and the ensuing retirement.
limits: Loss of the position does not quantify the delay.
No synchronized start/end clock or zero delay is imputed.
components.criterion_note: Conditional hold for a source-stated day or two.
components.success_criterion: Conditionally hold the position for a day or two while the wings join.

components.objective: Effect a junction of the two wings.
components.precedence_note: The junction is stated as the purpose of using the position.
components.observed_result: Damas reports that the other general joined with some troops while an advanced guard did not join.
components.result_window: Crati retirement and subsequent division of the retreat.
limits: Some joining is not no junction or a complete reassembly.
The OCR quotation was checked on the existing p. 396 image; no troops are summed.
components.criterion_note: Join the two wings; no complete population criterion is supplied.
components.success_criterion: Effect a junction of the two wings.

components.objective: Dispute the ground inch by inch as the only possible campaign object.
components.precedence_note: The wording is the author's after-reverse counterfactual assessment.
components.observed_result: The same account describes loss of the position and retreat; its counterfactual wording does not supply a prior grading rule.
limits: Do not recode a retrospective should-have judgment as a documented prior mandate.
components.criterion_note: No prior assigned success threshold is established.

components.objective: Force the British general to re-embark.
components.precedence_note: Koch narrates this expectation with the decision to attack; his alternative motive explanations are speculative.
components.observed_result: The reported battle ends in a French retreat, and Bunbury says the hope of destroying the British was ended.
components.result_window: The Maida battle action, not all later expedition outcomes.
limits: A later British departure would not by itself show this attack achieved its purpose.
Koch's printed action date and Bunbury/frozen entry date remain distinct.
components.success_criterion: Force the British general to re-embark.

components.objective: March at daylight to attack the enemy camp.
components.precedence_note: Bunbury places the reported order on the previous evening.
components.observed_result: Bunbury reports the advance and the French leaving their camp position for the plain; a battle followed.
components.result_window: The fourth-July advance and battle in Bunbury.
limits: A reported advance and victory do not prove a literal assault on the original camp.
The dated event reported in a memoir is not the supplied original order.
components.criterion_note: The specified advance and planned attack on the camp.
components.success_criterion: March at daylight to attack the enemy camp.

components.objective: Gain the left of the French position.
components.precedence_note: Bunbury reports this as the object of the advance.
components.observed_result: Bunbury reports the French moving from the original position and their left wing being overthrown.
limits: Overthrow of a left wing does not establish the exact planned geographical maneuver.
components.criterion_note: The intended flank/position geometry is not mapped.
components.success_criterion: Gain the left of the French position.

components.objective: Expect the landing to force Reynier to retreat to Catanzaro.
components.precedence_note: Bunbury recalls the belief formed before committing the expedition.
components.observed_result: Bunbury reports retreat by the road toward Catanzaro; Koch likewise reports retreat toward Catanzaro.
limits: This is qualified consistency of observed retreat with an expectation.
It does not establish an arrival time or identify the landing's causal effect.
Retreat toward Catanzaro is a qualified directional match, not a verified arrival or the whole expected chain.
components.criterion_note: A retreat in the stated direction; arrival and causation remain separate.

components.objective: Expect the insurrection in both provinces to become general.
components.precedence_note: This is another link in Bunbury's recalled conditional belief.
components.observed_result: A later Koch passage describes limited insurrection while discussing Gaëta; it does not establish the expected general extent.
limits: OCR-only geographical wording; no map/extent is inferred.
Neither the battle result nor this one later assertion grades the entire insurrection.
components.criterion_note: The provinces, extent threshold and success deadline are not operationalized.

components.objective: Expect Masséna to abandon the siege of Gaëta.
components.precedence_note: Bunbury recalls this expectation before the expedition.
components.observed_result: The Gaëta records instead report capitulation and subsequent French entry.
components.result_window: The continuing Gaëta episode through agreement on eighteenth July and entry on nineteenth July.
limits: This checks the stated relief expectation in that episode, not every possible temporary siege interruption.
Cross-entry evidence is one linked follow-through observation, not another Maida victory or Gaëta weight.
components.criterion_note: Relief by abandonment of the siege.
components.success_criterion: Masséna abandons the siege of Gaëta.

components.precedence_note: Koch reports the purpose during the siege before the later capture, not a proven initial appointment mandate.
components.observed_result: Colletta reports surrender on eighteenth July; Koch reports entry on nineteenth July.
limits: Capture is observed; its cost, value and causal commander share are not graded.
Capitulation terms preserve embarkation/non-service conditions rather than permanent destruction.
components.criterion_note: Reported surrender/occupation of the named place.

components.precedence_note: Colletta reports a council decision before the surrender.
components.observed_result: Surrender is reported, but the account does not establish how much it was accelerated or a success deadline.
components.result_window: The council decision and later surrender in Colletta.
limits: No counterfactual siege duration or arbitrary efficiency score is invented.
components.criterion_note: No required date or comparison duration is supplied.

components.objective: Use the besieging troops in the rebellious provinces.
components.precedence_note: This is the purpose Colletta attaches to hastening surrender.
components.observed_result: The place was surrendered; these adopted passages do not trace the stated body's subsequent deployment or provincial results.
limits: Surrender alone does not prove that the whole reported force was redeployed or pacification achieved.
This pilot does not reopen force-population or appointment extraction.
components.criterion_note: Actual release and use of the stated population in the provinces.
components.success_criterion: Use the besieging troops in the rebellious provinces.

components.objective: Prepare to defend Gaeta and refuse the regency's surrender direction, invoking higher commands.
components.precedence_note: Colletta places the preparation/refusal before the defence narrative. The general royal injunction is addressed to the regency; no supplied dated local order is established.
components.observed_result: Gaeta was defended and later capitulated. The reported royal instruction, governor's refusal and later council remain different authority/phase observations.
components.result_window: Early refusal, ensuing defence and later capitulation; no whole-siege appointment window selected.
limits: The source reports an earlier purpose, not merely observed later resistance.
The general instruction never to cede royal fortresses is not installed as the exclusive local commander's grading criterion.
Colletta's higher-command account and Koch's speculative explanation remain unreconciled.
components.criterion_note: The relation of the general royal/regency command to the governor's operative mission, acceptable surrender conditions and duration remains unestablished.

components.objective: Continue holding the place, as the late-siege council favored.
components.precedence_note: The council occurs after the siege has begun and before further resistance; it is not an opening mandate.
components.observed_result: The garrison later agreed to capitulation with conditional embarkation.
limits: Duration is OCR-only, with no pinned page 243 facsimile in the allowed set.
Colletta's earlier higher-command refusal and Koch's speculative origin explanation remain separate.
No mission failure follows automatically from eventual surrender; no exclusive commander is assigned.
components.criterion_note: A duration follows in the OCR as dix4iait jours*; no reliable normalized deadline is adopted.

components.objective: Reduce Amantea under the renewed attack dispositions.
components.precedence_note: Koch places final dispositions on fifteenth December before the source-reported eighteenth-December investment.
components.observed_result: Koch reports capitulation on sixth February; Colletta also reports surrender on honorable terms.
components.result_window: The renewed siege, within the frozen December 1806-February 1807 entry.
limits: Earlier failed attempts remain separate.
Koch's thirty-three days and Colletta's forty days excluding the first assault are not averaged or used as an efficiency denominator.
Conditional passage/non-service terms do not establish permanent force destruction.
components.criterion_note: Reported capitulation of the named place.
components.success_criterion: Reduce the named place under the renewed dispositions.

components.objective: Restore peace in the wider region by reducing insurgent bases.
components.precedence_note: Koch's narrative supplies a strategic rationale before the reduction; the underlying dated mandate is not supplied.
components.observed_result: Amantea's capitulation is reported, but regional pacification is not established by these passages.
components.result_window: Wider regional follow-through, outside the local capture alone.
limits: The source's necessary-condition claim is not proof of sufficiency.
The OCR-only rationale includes another town; no combined territorial or readiness score is created.
components.criterion_note: No complete area, durability criterion or deadline is supplied.

components.objective: A disposition to hold Amantea is inferred from continued resistance and fidelity language.
components.precedence_note: The adopted passages describe behavior and a letter exchange; they do not supply a prior operational order or success criterion.
components.observed_result: Colletta reports resistance, hunger and surrender on honorable terms.
components.result_window: Earlier attempts, renewed siege and capitulation remain distinguished.
limits: Resistance is not automatically a documented pre-action objective.
Capitulation does not establish whether an unrecorded delaying or preservation mission was achieved.
components.criterion_note: No explicit prior mandate, deadline or relief criterion is established.
